definition.opening: Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented knot diagram with ordered crossings $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ and a marked point $p$ away from crossings. Put $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ and $\mathbb F_2=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. At a resolution state $v\in\{0,1\}^n$, let $V_v$ be the free abelian group generated by the resolution circles, order its circle generators, and use the exterior algebra $\Lambda^*V_v$ as its state module. A wedge of $r$ distinct circle generators has circle quantum degree $k(v)-2r$, where $k(v)=\operatorname{rank}V_v$; its total normalized degrees are $i(v)=|v|-n_-$ and $q=|v|+n_+-2n_-+k(v)-2r$. For a merge saddle joining circles $C_1,C_2$, let $p:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ be the quotient sending both to the merged circle and fixing the other generators; the edge map is $\Lambda^*p$. For a split saddle replacing $C$ by $C_1,C_2$, let $j:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ send $C$ to $C_1$ and fix the other generators; the unsigned edge map is $z\mapsto(C_1-C_2)\wedge\Lambda^*j(z)$. Choosing $C_2$ instead of $C_1$ gives the same map, while reversing the order of $C_1,C_2$ changes only its sign. Multiply each edge map by a sign $\epsilon(e)\in\{1,-1\}$, incorporating any circle-generator reordering sign. The direct sum of these state modules with the resulting cube differential is the odd Khovanov cochain complex $C_o(D)$. Write $Z_p$ for the circle containing the mark. Use the right action $z\cdot X=z\wedge Z_p$, making $C_o(D)$ a complex of right $\mathbb A$-modules; since $\mathbb A$ is commutative these are also ordinary modules over that ring. The action has quantum degree $-2$.

The square condition is that the sum of the two signed saddle composites around each two-dimensional cube face is zero. An edge sign function satisfying it is called square-compatible; existence and invariance require separate proofs.

Let $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$, with $\deg_q(h)=\deg_q(X)=-2$. Its Frobenius structure has unit $\eta(1)=1$, counit $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$, quotient-ring multiplication, and comultiplication

Put $\mathbb B=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)=\mathbb R/(2,h)$. Modulo $2$, the odd exterior basis vector $C_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge C_{i_r}$ corresponds to the even tensor state labeling the selected circles $C_{i_j}$ by $X$ and all other circles by $1$. This statewise bijection defines the candidate comparison $f_D:C_o(D)\otimes\mathbb F_2\to C_h(D)\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb B$ after setting $h=0$.

A **local even–odd (LEO) triple** is a triple $(C,D,f)$ consisting of a finitely generated bigraded cochain complex $C$ free over $\mathbb A$, a finitely generated bigraded cochain complex $D$ free over $\mathbb R$, and a bigraded $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain homotopy equivalence

A local map $(C,D,f)\to(C',D',f')$ is a pair of bigraded module chain maps $\alpha:C\to C'$ and $\beta:D\to D'$ such that $\beta[h^{-1}]$ is a chain homotopy equivalence and the square induced by $f,f',\alpha,\beta$ after quotienting by $(2,h)$ commutes up to an $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain homotopy. Two LEO triples are locally equivalent when there is a local map in each direction.
